questions.question: Explain why (3x²)² = 9x⁴ and not 3x⁴ or 6x⁴.
questions.expected_answer: The exponent outside the bracket applies to every factor inside: 3² = 9 and (x²)² = x⁴. Writing 3x⁴ forgets to square the 3; writing 6x⁴ doubles it instead of squaring it. Check x = 1: (3)² = 9.

questions.question: How is √(25x⁶) found, and how do you check it?
questions.expected_answer: Root the coefficient (√25 = 5) and halve the exponent (6 ÷ 2 = 3): 5x³. Check by squaring: (5x³)² = 25x⁶.

questions.question: Why must 16x² + 9x² be collected before the square root is taken?
questions.expected_answer: Roots do not distribute over sums. Collecting gives 25x², whose root is 5x. Taking roots separately gives 4x + 3x = 7x, which is wrong: at x = 1, √25 = 5 ≠ 7.
